learning_outcomes.text: The student acquires knowledge regarding: The fundamental principles of automatic systems (structure, classification, operation).
Mathematical models for describing and analyzing dynamic systems.
Bases of automatic control theory (functional blocks, stability, performance).
Types of sensors, actuators and execution elements used in mechanical, mechatronic and robotic systems.
The student can develop skills in: Modeling and simulating the behavior of simple automatic systems.
Analyzing the response of systems (in time and frequency).
Proposing and dimensioning control elements to meet specifications.
Using simulation software to verify solutions.
The student applies criteria, evaluation methods, concepts from automatic systems theory in the design of industrial equipment.
The student/graduate develops responsibilities and learns to become autonomous.
Responsibility by: Ensuring the safe and efficient operation of automatic systems.
Respecting technical and ethical standards in system design.
Documenting and presenting the results of analyses and projects.
Autonomy by: Identifying control problems and selecting appropriate resolution methods.
Continuous development of knowledge through individual study and experimentation.

syllabus_topics: Information - a component of automatic/mechatronic systems
Objectives and purpose of the discipline; connection with other disciplines;
Automation in engineering education and practice. Trends.
Examples of automatic/mechatronic products and systems (industrial robot, hard disk, automobile)
Unit step signal: definition, response, examples
Unit impulse signal (Dirac): definition, properties, response, examples
4. Calculation Methods and Techniques in Systems Theory
Time domain calculation techniques (impulse succession; convolution)
Calculation techniques based on Laplace transform
Graphical representations of the transfer function: Nyquist diagram; Bode diagram
Operations with transfer functions: series connection, parallel connection, inverse feedback connection
Fourier series: role and importance in automatic systems theory, examples
Notion of state and state space, choice of state variables
Example of using state variables in the analysis of a technical system
Techniques based on the sampling theorem
Transfer function of systems with sampling
Stability of linear systems (fundamental stability criterion, Routh-Hurwitz criterion, Nyquist criterion - advantages)
Necessity of system modeling and identification
Control laws (proportional P, integral I, proportional-integral PI, proportional-derivative PD, PID)
9. Hardware Structure of an Automatic System

Description of specific elements: definitions, role and functionality (microprocessor, microcontroller, memory unit UM, central processing unit CPU, data and address bus, input-output system I/O, timer unit, analog-digital converter).
Media presentation of mechatronic systems (robots, computing technology, modern automobile, mechatronics in medicine, architecture of an intelligent machine, applications - MEMS)
1. Systems and signals; convolutions; approximations of the 8 function. Applications in LabView.
2. Transfer functions; hard disk modeling; automobile suspension modeling. Applications in Lab View.
3. Analysis of system time response: unit step response, unit impulse response, harmonic input response; performance specifications on time response. Applications in Lab View.
4. Frequency representation of systems; hodographs; Bode diagram; Applications in Lab View.
5. Series, parallel, feedback connections. Stability analysis in closed loop based on Nyquist criterion. Applications in LabView.
6. Constructive-functional study of an automatic positioning system. Evaluation of dynamic parameters of an automobile with Lab View.
teaching_methods: Participatory lectures and debates based on Power Point presentations, which will be made available to students. Presentations contain images and sketches to make the information easier to understand and assimilate. Each course will begin with a brief recap of concepts covered in the previous course.
In the laboratory, simulation software is used for identifying and verifying solutions.

The teaching method is thus based on discovery learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling), as well as on action-based methods such as exercise, practical activities and problem-solving.
assessment_rules: Solving completely defined problems of medium complexity from the fundamental domain studied, obtaining a passing score (minimum 5) for both the course and the laboratory.
